profileNotes: Primary goals: morning or early-day cardio for activation/ADHD support, lower body fat, larger glutes, stronger core, improved pelvic and rib-cage control, general mobility, lateral movement, and modestly greater front-facing hip/lower-body presence through quads, upper/outer glutes, outer thighs, and adductors.
Home-oriented plan without machines. Compound lower-body movements are preferred over isolated abductions.
Physical therapy for a cervical disc bulge already supplies most upper-body work. The PT program takes priority over this generic structure.
Kettlebell halos are excluded from unsupervised routines because they reliably restart numbness, even though the therapist previously said this was acceptable.
Stop and report any exercise that causes or increases numbness, tingling, radiating arm pain, weakness, dizziness, unusual headache, hand clumsiness, or worsening balance.
RDLs and other exercises involving handheld weights are conditional on the loading position remaining symptom-free and being acceptable to the physical therapist.
The labels 'Morristown' and 'Flemington' may identify particular handout versions; exact technique should match the therapist's demonstration.

exercises.name: Walking
exercises.notes: Includes brisk walking for regular cardio and gentle walking for recovery. Begin very easily and increase pace gradually.

exercises.name: Marching in Place
exercises.notes: Used as a short general warm-up or minimum-success cardio option.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.notes: Conversational effort; may substitute for walking on Wednesday or another cardio day.

exercises.name: Low-Impact Dance Cardio
exercises.notes: May emphasize comfortable side-to-side movement. Keep impact low unless higher impact has been cleared and feels appropriate.

exercises.name: Step-Touch
exercises.notes: Low-impact lateral pattern for cardio warm-ups or dance cardio.

exercises.name: Grapevine
exercises.notes: Optional lateral coordination pattern for dance cardio.

exercises.name: Standing Scapular Forward-and-Back Glide
exercises.notes: With arms relaxed, gently let the shoulder blades travel forward around the ribs and then slightly backward. Do not shrug or forcefully pinch them together. This is not the same exercise as a serratus wall slide.

exercises.name: Wall Angel
exercises.notes: Use a comfortable range. Do not force the head, hands, or lower back against the wall. Warm-up version uses 5 small-range repetitions.

exercises.name: Serratus Wall Slide
exercises.notes: Press forearms gently into the wall and slide upward while allowing the shoulder blades to rotate up and around the ribs. Mild core engagement is expected. Avoid excessive shrugging, rib flare, back arching, or holding the breath. Warm-up version uses 5 unresisted repetitions.

exercises.name: Theraband Row
exercises.notes: Anchor around chest or lower-rib height. Pull elbows toward the ribs with relaxed shoulders and a neutral neck. Do not lean backward or crane the head. Warm-up version is unresisted or uses a very light band for 8 repetitions.

exercises.name: Theraband Reverse W
exercises.notes: Used as Monday's face-pull-type variation. Exact hand and arm position should match the PT handout because a reverse W is not always identical to a conventional face pull.

exercises.name: Cable-Column Face Pull
exercises.notes: Used on Friday instead of the reverse W. Warm-up version rehearses the face-pull motion without resistance for 6–8 repetitions. Avoid jutting the head forward.

exercises.name: Cheerleaders
exercises.notes: Band-based horizontal and diagonal pulling series. Use exactly the directions and technique demonstrated by the physical therapist.

exercises.name: Upper-Trapezius Stretch
exercises.notes: Keep it gentle; avoid aggressive neck pulling or forceful range.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
exercises.notes: The exact 'Morristown' version is unknown. Only use the overhead position if it remains free of neurological symptoms.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo
exercises.notes: Reliably restarts numbness. Do not perform unsupervised until the therapist watches the response and defines acceptable intensity, distribution, duration, and stopping rules.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.notes: Counts toward both core strength and pelvic-control goals. The exact Flemington variation should match the therapist's handout.

exercises.name: Heel Tap
exercises.status: optional; superseded by PT dead bugs
exercises.notes: Originally proposed as a dead-bug variation. Not required on days when prescribed dead bugs are performed.

exercises.name: Kneeling Side Plank
exercises.notes: Arm-loading and neck position should be cleared with the physical therapist before use.

exercises.name: Band Pallof Press
exercises.notes: Anti-rotation core option. Keep ribs stacked and neck neutral.

exercises.name: 90/90 Breathing with Gentle Pelvic Tuck
exercises.notes: Used for rib-cage and pelvic control. The goal is gentle positioning and breathing, not forcing the lower back flat all day.

exercises.name: Relaxed Breathing
exercises.notes: Breathe without shrugging the shoulders. Used in cardio and recovery warm-ups.

exercises.name: Standing Pelvic Tilt
exercises.notes: Slowly practice anterior and posterior pelvic movement without using the upper body to compensate.

exercises.name: Alternating Knee Raise
exercises.notes: Controlled standing knee lift used before mobility work.

exercises.name: Hip Circle
exercises.notes: Start with small controlled circles. Use support as needed.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge to Wall
exercises.notes: Practice sending the hips backward while maintaining a neutral neck and controlled torso.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Primary Tuesday lift. Keep weights close, send hips backward, stack ribs, and let the neck follow the spine. Stop the descent when the hips stop traveling backward. Warm-up set uses bodyweight or substantially lighter dumbbells for 6–8 repetitions.

exercises.name: Staggered-Stance Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Thursday unilateral hinge. Most weight stays through the front leg; the rear foot acts as a kickstand. Warm-up version is bodyweight or very light for 5–6 per side.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Used to rehearse the goblet-squat pattern before loading.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Tuesday compound movement for quads, adductors, glutes, and greater front-facing lower-body presence. Holding weight at the chest must remain symptom-free.

exercises.name: Chair Squat / Sit-to-Stand
exercises.notes: Originally used as a beginner squat and later as supported squat practice on recovery day.

exercises.name: Supported Deep Squat Hold
exercises.notes: Recovery or mobility option. May be replaced with sit-to-stand practice.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Tuesday option in place of hip thrust and optional Saturday finisher at 12–15 repetitions. Warm-up version uses bodyweight for 10 repetitions.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.notes: Tuesday alternative to the glute bridge. Keep neck positioning comfortable and avoid loading arrangements that provoke arm or hand symptoms.

exercises.name: Frog Pump
exercises.notes: Originally proposed as a glute-bridge variation in the starter Glutes B routine; not part of the current week.

exercises.name: Banded Lateral Walk
exercises.notes: Previously used on Tuesday for lateral stability, then replaced by goblet squats to favor compound lower-body training. Progress by slowing the steps or using a stronger band.

exercises.name: Standing Banded Hip Abduction
exercises.notes: Previously included for side-glute work but removed when the plan shifted away from isolated abduction exercises.

exercises.name: Supported Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Originally proposed in Glutes B. Not part of the current week but remains a possible unilateral alternative.

exercises.name: Supported Split Squat
exercises.notes: May occasionally replace goblet squats rather than being added. This preserves workout length while adding quad and glute work.

exercises.name: Supported Lateral Lunge
exercises.notes: Thursday compound movement for adductors, quads, glutes, lateral strength, and front-facing lower-body presence. Increase comfortable depth first, then repetitions, then load. Warm-up version uses 5 shallow repetitions per side.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Up
exercises.equipment: low stable step; optional support and dumbbells
exercises.notes: Stand sideways to the step, place the nearer foot fully on it, drive through that foot to rise, and lower slowly. Targets quads and side/upper glutes. Reach 12 controlled repetitions before increasing either step height or load, not both.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Down
exercises.notes: Saturday movement-quality drill. Lower under control and keep the pelvis, knee, and foot aligned.

exercises.name: Cossack Weight Shift
exercises.notes: Saturday lateral mobility and adductor-strength practice. Keep it shallow enough to control the descent and return. Increase range and control before adding weight.

exercises.name: Low-Impact Skater Step
exercises.notes: No jumping initially. Use narrow, controlled steps and increase speed or reach only after balance is solid. Warm-up version uses 5 slow taps per side.

exercises.name: Side Step
exercises.notes: Simple unloaded side steps before Saturday lateral training.

exercises.name: Supported Lateral Weight Shift
exercises.notes: Shift weight side to side while testing hip, knee, inner-thigh, and balance comfort before lateral work.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip-Flexor Stretch
exercises.notes: Use a gentle posterior pelvic tuck rather than arching the lower back.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.notes: Controlled internal and external hip-rotation mobility drill.

exercises.name: Adductor Rock-Back
exercises.notes: Rock backward slowly to mobilize the inner thigh and groin without forcing the range.

exercises.name: Ankle Rock
exercises.notes: Keep the heel planted while the knee moves forward comfortably.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch
exercises.notes: May substitute for ankle rocks during mobility sessions.

exercises.name: Chair Pose
exercises.notes: Suggested as a yoga movement that could fit the recovery or mobility day if neck position remains comfortable.

exercises.name: Warrior Pose Variation

progressionRules.rule: When every working set reaches the top of the repetition range with a controlled hinge, neutral neck, several good repetitions still available, and no symptom increase, add a small amount of weight.
Build from 8 toward 12 repetitions. When all three sets reach 12 with consistent depth and control, add a small amount of weight and return to 8–9 repetitions.
Increase comfortable depth first, then repetitions, and finally load. Do not increase all three simultaneously.
Begin with a low stable step. Reach 12 controlled repetitions before increasing either the load or step height; change only one variable at a time.
Increase range and control before adding weight. This may remain a mobility-oriented movement rather than becoming a heavy lift.
Increase speed or lateral reach only after balance and landing control are solid. Jumping is not required.
If returned to the plan, progress with slower controlled steps or a stronger band.

Begin with light resistance and several good repetitions in reserve. After reaching the top of the range for two sessions with clean form and no meaningful symptom increase during or afterward, add repetitions or use the next-smallest resistance increase, not both at once. Confirm intended frequency and dosage with the physical therapist.

Stop if the movement causes or increases numbness, tingling, radiating pain, weakness, dizziness, unusual headache, hand clumsiness, or worsening balance. Do not repeatedly provoke a symptom merely to test whether it is still present.
